column1: So yesterday, I'm eatin' one of my wife's bagels (no lox, 'cause she forgot ta go to the deli), and I'm usin' this napkin.  I THINK it's clean, right?...
column2: 昨天啦，我在吃我老婆做的貝果（沒帶鮭魚卵，因為她忘記去熟食店拿），我用這個餐巾紙。我覺得沒髒啦？...

column1: Your bettin' on WHO in the super bowl?   Are you CRAZY?  Are you INSANE?  Ya wanna kill yourself, let me do it.  It'll be quicker.
column2: 你在賭誰贏超級盃？你瘋了嗎？你精神有問題嗎？想死的話讓我來。我手比較快。

column1: That's Leon.  He's a great Coroner, but the guy has a sick sense of humor.
column2: 那是 Leon。他是個好法醫，不過這傢伙幽默感很扭曲。

column1: One murder's enough for this dark alley, don't you think?
column2: 一宗命案對這條黑巷子夠了吧，你不覺得？

column1: You really like to flash those credentials, don't you?
column2: 你很喜歡亮警徽嘛？

column1: Don't you want to log the information about Andrew Dent in your notebook first?
column2: 你不想先把 Andrew Dent 的資料記進筆記本？

column1: That's nice, Bonds, but I only care for that stuff when it's still on the body.  Save it for L.P.D evidence.
column2: 不錯，Bonds，但我只在東西還在屍體上時才在乎。留著當 Lytton 警局的證物吧。

column1: Ah!  Would that the dead COULD speak!
column2: 啊！要是死人能說話就好了！

column1: You think about shooting the murder victim, but he's ALREADY DEAD!
column2: 你想朝命案被害人開槍，但他已經死了！

column1: You identify yourself to the stiff, then contemplate a long vacation.
column2: 你向屍體報上身分，然後幻想著度假。

column1: The car's been abandoned for some time.  There's nothing of interest in there.
column2: 那部車被棄置有一陣子了。裡面沒什麼有價值的。

column1: You don't need another sample.
column2: 你不需要再拿樣本了。

column1: You carefully scrape some of the gold paint transfer from the side of the white car along with a little white paint into the paper envelope.
column2: 你小心地把白車側面的金色油漆轉移跡象和少量白漆刮進紙信封。

column1: You need to use the proper field equipment to take a clean paint sample.
column2: 你得用適當的現場勘查工具才能拿到乾淨的油漆樣本。

column1: You don't have the field equipment necessary to take a clean paint sample.
column2: 你沒有拿乾淨油漆樣本所需的現場勘查工具。

column1: You don't need to worry about the garage.
column2: 你不必擔心修車廠。

column1: The uniformed officer will remove the tape when the body has been removed and the crime lab is finished with the area.
column2: 等屍體移走、鑑識組也勘查完現場，那位警員就會把膠帶撕掉。

column1: You need to give the license to the coroner first.
column2: 你得先把駕照給法醫。

column1: Using the toothpick, you scrape under the victim's fingernails.  You then place the collected skin and hair into a sample envelope.
column2: 你用牙籤在被害人指甲下方刮擦。然後把蒐集到的皮膚和毛髮放進樣本信封。

column1: You look carefully at the knife wounds in the upper chest.  Not a pretty sight.  But it's the pentagram carved into the flesh that really hits you between the eyes.
column2: 你仔細看著上胸部的刀傷。不是什麼美麗的景象。但是刻在肉裡的五芒星才真的讓你眼前一亮。

column1: Not another one!... you mutter.
column2: 「又來一個！」...你低聲抱怨。

column1: That's all Lytton needs - some freaked-out serial killer that thinks he's got a hot-line to Satan!
column2: 「Lytton 還需要什麼——一個精神錯亂的連續殺人犯以為自己能直通撒旦！」

column1: A bloody shirt covers the upper torso.
column2: 一件沾滿血跡的襯衫蓋住上身。

column1: You already have the hair and skin sample.
column2: 你已經有毛髮和皮膚樣本了。

column1: That is a good idea, but you'll need the proper equipment.
column2: 主意不錯，但你需要適當的工具。

column1: That's a good idea, but you'll need to use the proper field equipment.
column2: 主意不錯，但你得用適當的現場勘查工具。

column1: Looking closely at the victim's hands, you notice what appears to be hair and skin imbedded under the fingernails.
column2: 看著被害人的手，你注意到指甲下方像是嵌著毛髮和皮膚。

column1: Looks like somebody attacked this guy with toothpicks.
column2: 看起來有人用牙籤攻擊這傢伙。

column1: You carefully write down the information in your notebook.
column2: 你小心地把資訊寫進筆記本。

column1: You carefully search the body and remove the victim's identification.
column2: 你仔細搜查屍體並取走被害人的身分證件。

column1: There's nothing more in the victim's pockets.
column2: 被害人口袋裡沒有其他東西了。

column1: You examine the knife wounds in the upper chest.   Leon will be able to tell you more about the wounds in the Coroner's report.
column2: 你檢查上胸部的刀傷。Leon 會在法醫報告裡告訴你更多關於傷口的事。

column1: That's a nasty habit!
column2: 那可真是個壞習慣！

column1: I don't think he'd care to have his teeth picked right now.
column2: 我不覺得他現在會樂意被人挑牙齒。

column1: You have plenty of trash at home.
column2: 你家裡有一堆垃圾。

column1: The back entrance to the bar seems to be locked.
column2: 酒吧的後面入口好像被鎖住了。

column1: Morales ignores your attempt at conversation.
column2: Morales 忽視你試圖交談的嘗試。

column1: This car looks like the suspect vehicle we've been looking for.
column2: 這部車看起來像我們在找的嫌疑車輛。

column1: Hmmmm... no tags, though.
column2: 嗯...不過沒有牌照。

column1: You wander around for a moment and realize that there's nothing else of interest in this part of town.
column2: 你逛了一會兒，發現這一帶沒有其他有趣的東西。

column1: You curse as you watch the suspect getting away.
column2: 你眼看著嫌犯逃脫，忍不住罵了起來。

column1: What... What's going on?
column2: 怎...怎麼回事？

column1: Just get in the car!
column2: 快上車！

column1: You can't take a paint sample without the proper field equipment.
column2: 你沒有適當的現場勘查工具，不能拿油漆樣本。

column1: You can't search the inside of the car without a warrant.
column2: 沒有搜索票，你不能搜查車子內部。

column1: You look at the parked car and notice that the license plates are missing.  The car matches the description of the suspect vehicle.
column2: 你看著停著的車，注意到牌照不見了。這部車符合嫌疑車輛的描述。

column1: Giving the car a closer look, you see what appears to be a fresh white paint transfer.
column2: 仔細看那部車，你看到了好像是新鮮的白色油漆轉移跡象。

column1: Bingo, you mutter, "I got you now, you S.O.B..."
column2: 「答對了」，你低聲說，「我抓到你了，你混蛋...」

column1: You inspect the suspect car once more, and find no evidence other than the paint transfer.
column2: 你再檢查一次嫌疑車，除了油漆轉移跡象外沒有其他證物。

column1: You plant the tracking device on the suspect vehicle.
column2: 你在嫌疑車上安裝追蹤裝置。

column1: You carefully scrape some of the white paint transfer off and put it in an envelope.
column2: 你小心地把一些白色油漆轉移跡象刮下來放進信封。

column1: You don't need any more paint.
column2: 你不需要更多油漆了。

column1: The car won't fit in the envelope.
column2: 車子塞不進信封。

column1: You need to get the paint sample before you can store it in an envelope.
column2: 你得先拿到油漆樣本才能放進信封。

column1: Rubber's just rubber.  If you want some there's easier ways to get it than scraping it off the street.
column2: 橡膠就是橡膠。你要的話有比從街道上刮下來更簡單的辦法。

column1: There is no apparent need for anything in the trunk right now.
column2: 現在沒有明顯的理由需要整理行李廂的東西。

column1: Convinced that the serial killer will strike here next, you decide to stick around.
column2: 確信連續殺人犯下一個會在這裡作案，你決定留下來。

column1: If you want a drink, you'd have better luck inside.
column2: 你要喝東西的話在裡面運氣比較好。

column1: Better keep it holstered until you REALLY need it.
column2: 最好把它插在槍套裡，直到你真的需要。

column1: Hmmm... nothing of interest back here.
column2: 「嗯...這後面沒什麼有意思的。」

column1: I'm gonna check out the back for the suspect, Sonny.
column2: 我要去後面找嫌犯，Sonny。

column1: Hey that guy kinda looks familiar.
column2: 嘿，那傢伙看起來有點眼熟。

column1: The punk's hateful glare burns right through you.
column2: 那小子充滿仇恨的眼光刺穿你。

column1: You look carefully at the man. He closely matches the bag lady's physical description of the suspect in Marie's stabbing.
column2: 你仔細看著那個人。他的身體特徵跟流浪漢描述的 Marie 刺傷事件嫌犯非常相符。

column1: As you turn to ask the pool player about the vehicle...
column2: 當你轉身想問撞球玩家關於那部車...

column1: If you want something from the man why don't you just ask.
column2: 你想從那傢伙那裡得到什麼的話直接問啊。

column1: Approaching a potentially armed suspect, unprepared is not advisable.
column2: 未加準備地接近可能武裝的嫌犯是不明智的。

column1: Maybe I'd have better luck getting her attention when she isn't quite so busy.
column2: 也許我在她沒那麼忙的時候比較容易引起她的注意。

column1: You know anything about that car parked out front?
column2: 你知不知道外面停著的那部車？

column1: My customer's cars are their own business.
column2: 我客人的車那是他們自己的事。

column1: Okay, thanks.
column2: 好的，謝謝。

column1: What can I do for ya tonight?
column2: 今晚有什麼我可以幫你的嗎？

column1: Nothing. Thanks.
column2: 沒有。謝謝。

column1: Hey pal! If yer not buyin' booze, yer just takin' up real estate!
column2: 嘿，老兄！你不買酒的話就是白佔地皮！

column1: If you wanna order a drink then order it.
column2: 你要點飲料的話就點吧。

column1: I ain't got time for idle chit chat right now!
column2: 我現在沒時間閒聊！

column1: The man playing pool hasn't done anything wrong, except be rude.
column2: 那個打撞球的傢伙除了粗魯以外沒有做錯什麼。

column1: He's waiting for his pool partner to finish his turn.
column2: 他在等他的撞球夥伴輪到他玩。

column1: The man playing pool looks like a rough customer. You wonder where his pool partner is.
column2: 那個打撞球的傢伙看起來是個粗人。你不知道他的撞球夥伴在哪裡。

column1: Maybe you should wait until he makes his shot first.
column2: 也許你應該等他先打一桿。

column1: The man ignores you. He seems to be waiting on someone to come finish the game.
column2: 那個人忽視你。他好像在等有人來完成這場遊戲。

column1: You think about busting the guy's head, but you restrain yourself.
column2: 你想著砸這傢伙的頭，但你忍住了。

column1: Is that your car out front?
column2: 外面的車是你的嗎？

column1: *Sniff* Anybody else in here smell bacon?
column2: *嗅* 還有人聞到警察了嗎？

column1: Why on earth would you want to do that?!
column2: 你究竟為什麼要那樣做？！

column1: He seems harmless enough. You decide to leave him alone.
column2: 他看起來夠無害的。你決定不理他。

column1: The guy hasn't done anything wrong.
column2: 那傢伙沒有做錯什麼。

column1: Excuse me, Sir. is that your car parked right out front?
column2: 不好意思，先生。外面停著的車是你的嗎？

column1: Naw! My car's been in the shop all week. Why?
column2: 不是！我的車整週都在修車廠。幹嘛？

column1: Nothing. thanks.
column2: 沒事。謝謝。

column1: The guy's busy drowning his sorrows and doesn't pay any attention to you.
column2: 那傢伙正忙著借酒澆愁，沒在理你。

column1: He hasn't done anything wrong. Leave him alone.
column2: 他沒有做錯什麼。別理他。

column1: Excuse me sir, is that your car parked right out front?
column2: 不好意思，先生，外面停著的車是你的嗎？

column1: Not me. I drive a Harley man!
column2: 不是我。我騎哈雷機車！

column1: Sorry to bother you.
column2: 抱歉打擾了。

column1: Touching the pool table while someone is playing isn't a good idea.
column2: 有人在玩撞球時碰撞球台不是個好主意。

column1: If you want a drink just order one.
column2: 你要喝東西就點一杯吧。

column1: Ahh... if you only had time!
column2: 啊...要是你有時間就好！

column1: You don't have time to watch television.
column2: 你沒有時間看電視。

column1: You wouldn't take one of those tacky candles if somebody paid you.
column2: 就算有人付錢你也不會拿那些俗氣的蠟燭。

column1: No thanks, you don't smoke.
column2: 不用了，你不抽菸。

column1: The door is locked.
column2: 門被鎖了。

column1: You decide to drive to the hospital to check up on marie.
column2: 你決定開車去醫院看 Marie。

column1: This is the front entrance to the coroner's office.
column2: 這是法醫辦公室的前面入口。

column1: Your car sits out in front of the coroner's office.
column2: 你的車停在法醫辦公室的外面。

column1: You haven't even been inside yet!
column2: 你還沒進去過！

column1: The trunk of your car is closed.
column2: 你的車行李廂是關著的。

column1: Since you're not a dog, I'll ignore that request.
column2: 既然你不是狗，我就忽視那個要求。

column1: Not having a green thumb, you leave the tree alone.
column2: 沒有園藝天賦，你就別管那棵樹了。

column1: There's nothing you can do with the sign.
column2: 你沒辦法對那個標誌做什麼。

column1: There's nothing you can do with the sidewalk.
column2: 你沒辦法對人行道做什麼。

column1: Ok Bonds,... Lets try and keep our mind on our work!
column2: 好的，Bonds...我們專心工作吧！

column1: You decide to stick around until the coroner shows up.
column2: 你決定留下來等法醫出現。

column1: Oh yeah, I almost forgot Rocklin's personal effects.
column2: 「哦是啦，我差點忘了 Rocklin 的私人物品。」

column1: Well, if it isn't Sergeant 'B'.  I hadda hunch you might show up.
column2: 哦，如果不是警佐 B。我就猜你可能會出現。

column1: You might find this amusing.  I found it on your dead suspect.  Looks like you have a fan.
column2: 你可能會覺得有趣。我在你那具死屍上找到它。看起來你有個粉絲。

column1: With a sinking feeling, you recognize the old news article covering your promotion.
column2: 心下一沉，你認出了那篇報導你升職的舊新聞。

column1: A red marking pen pentagram mars your photograph.
column2: 紅色簽字筆的五芒星毀掉了你的照片。

column1: I wouldn't worry about it,\nBonds.  You look GOOD in red.
column2: 我不會擔心，\nBonds。你穿紅色看起來很棒。

column1: Not to worry.  I've got a positive I.D. on your stiff.  Name's Steven Rocklin.  Last known address is 500 West Peach.
column2: 別擔心。我有你那具屍體的確切身分。叫 Steven Rocklin。最後已知地址是 West Peach 500 號。
